newsitem.title: UK: After one year 15 pct homes left former British Gas.
newsitem.headline: After one year 15 pct homes left former British Gas.

text.p: On the first anniversary of domestic competition in the British gas market, nearly 15 percent of eligible households have switched suppliers and are no longer customers of British Gas or its successor Centrica, industry regulator Ofgas said.

The first pilot area, covering Devon, Cornwall and Somerset opened to competition on April 29 last year. This was followed by a second pilot in Avon, Dorset, Kent and East and West Sussex, which opened in two phases in February and March this year.

A total of 293,951 households in the pilot areas have switched, out of around 2 million domestic consumers. This breaks down to 104,182 in the first pilot area and 189,769 in the second, according to Ofgas' latest figures from last Friday.

The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) announced in March that competition would be extended throughout the rest of Britain in stages by April 1998, starting with Scotland and the North East of England in October.
But opposition Labour's energy spokesman John Battle told Reuters on Monday that if Labour forms a government it will not be tied to the same timetable.
"We're not interested in slowing down competition but...what's worrying us is that the lessons of the southwest have not yet been learnt in terms of consumer' rights," he said.
